prompt_text: Who does backflow testing and repair near Liberty MO?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t browse the web from here, so I can’t give a current list of businesses. I can, however, tell you the fastest ways to find qualified backflow testers and what to check so you hire the right person in/near Liberty, MO — and I can draft a call/email script or help you evaluate any businesses you find.

Where to look
- Call the City of Liberty Water/Public Works department and ask for their list of approved backflow testers or for requirements for tester certification and test report submission. Many utilities keep a preferred/approved list.
- Google Maps or Apple Maps: search “backflow testing Liberty MO” or “backflow tester near Liberty, MO.”
- Review sites: Yelp, Angi (Angie’s List), Thumbtack, Nextdoor and Facebook Marketplace/community groups.
- Search for local plumbing companies, irrigation companies, or fire protection companies that advertise “backflow testing” or “cross-connection control.”
- Professional organizations: American Backflow Prevention Association (ABPA) and local plumbing/irrigation trade groups sometimes list certified testers.

What to check before hiring
- Certification: ask for the tester’s backflow tester certification (often called Backflow Assembly Tester, BAT, or similar). Confirm it’s current and recognized by the local utility or state.
- Insurance and license: verify general liability and any required state/city plumber’s license.
- Experience with your device type: tell them whether your assembly is an RPZ (reduced-pressure zone), double-check valve assembly (DCVA), pressure vacuum breaker (PVB), or irrigation/backflow model.
- Will they submit the test report to the City/utility? Some municipalities require testers to file the report directly.
- Price and turnaround: typical residential tests often run ~$60–$150 (varies). Repairs are extra — get an estimate/quote for parts and labor.
- Warranties/parts: ask if they use OEM parts and if repairs are guaranteed.
- References/reviews: quick online check or ask for local references.

Who typically does this
- Licensed plumbers (many offer testing/repair)
- Landscape irrigation companies (especially for irrigation assemblies)
- Fire protection/service companies (for fire-line backflow assemblies)
- Companies that advertise “cross-connection control” or “backflow prevention”

If you want, I can:
- Draft a short phone script or email you can use to contact companies or the City of Liberty Water Department.
- Evaluate a few provider names/quotes if you paste them here.
- Search for businesses now if you paste the results/links you find and want help choosing.
